dataset.name: City Owned Real Estate Inventory Parcels: Live
dataset.description:
Dataset Summary
Please note: this data is live (updated nightly) to reflect the latest changes in the City's systems of record.

About the Data:
For a data dictionary / codebook, click here.

This dataset is a polygon feature layer with the boundaries of all tax parcels owned by the City of Rochester. This includes all public parks, and municipal buildings, as well as vacant land and structures currently owned by the City. The data includes fields with features about each property including property type, date of sale, whether the property is expected to be sold, land value, dimensions, and more.

To view a interactive map that features this layer, please visit:
https://maps.cityofrochester.gov/portal/apps/webappviewer/index.html?id=eecba714701449c69054851c9ac57198

About City Owned Properties:
The City's real estate inventory is managed by the Division of Real Estate in the Department of Neighborhood and Business Development. Properties like municipal buildings and parks are expected to be in long term ownership of the City. Properties such as vacant land and vacant structures are ones the City is actively seeking to reposition for redevelopment to increase the City's tax base and economic activity. The City acquires many of these properties through the tax foreclosure auction process when no private entity bids the minimum bid. Some of these properties stay in the City's ownership for years, while others are quickly sold to development partners. 

For more information please visit the City's webpage for the Division of Real Estate: 
https://www.cityofrochester.gov/realestate/

dataset.name: NYC Zoning Tax Lot Database
dataset.description: The Zoning Tax Lot Database is a comma-separated values (CSV) file that contains up-to-date zoning by parcel. The Database includes the zoning designations and zoning map associated with a specific tax block and lot. The Database is updated on a monthly basis to reflect rezoning and corrections to the file. All previously released versions of this data are available on the DCP Website: BYTES of the BIG APPLE. Current version: 20260930

columns.name: Borough Code
columns.description:
The borough that the tax lot is located in.

(1=Manhattan, 2=Bronx, 3=Brooklyn, 4=Queens, 5=Staten Island)

columns.name: Tax Block
columns.description:
The tax block that the tax lot is located in.

This field contains a one to five digit tax block number which is preceded with
leading blanks when the tax block is less than five digits.

Each tax block is unique within a borough (see BOROUGH).

columns.name: Tax Lot
columns.description:
The number of the tax lot.

This field contains a one to four digit tax lot number which is preceded with
leading blanks when the tax lot is less than four digits.

Each tax lot is unique within a tax block (see TAX BLOCK).

columns.name: BBL
columns.description:
A concatenation of the borough code, tax block and tax lot.

This field consists of the borough code followed by the tax block followed by the tax lot.  The borough code is one numeric digit.  The tax block is one to five numeric digits, preceded with leading zeros when the block is less than five digits.  The tax lot is one to four digits and is preceded with leading zeros when the lot is less than four digits.

For condominiums, the BBL is for the billing lot. See TAX LOT for more information on how condominiums are handled.

Examples:
Manhattan Borough Code 1, Tax Block 16, Tax Lot 100 would be stored as 1000160100.
Brooklyn Borough Code 3, Tax Block 15828, Tax Lot 7501 would be stored as 3158287501.

columns.name: Zoning District 1
columns.description:
The zoning district classification of the tax lot or in a limited number
of cases the Zoning Resolution section number that pertains to special requirements
for selected properties in Queens.

columns.name: Zoning District 2
columns.description:
If the tax lot is divided by zoning boundary lines, ZONING DISTRICT
2 represents the zoning classification occupying the second greatest percentage
of the tax lot's area.

columns.name: Zoning District 3
columns.description:
If the tax lot is divided by zoning boundary lines, ZONING DISTRICT
3 represents the zoning classification occupying the third greatest percentage
of the tax lot's area.

columns.name: Zoning District 4
columns.description:
If the tax lot is divided by zoning boundary lines, ZONING DISTRICT
4 represents the zoning classification occupying the fourth greatest percentage
of the tax lot's area.

columns.name: Commercial Overlay 1
columns.description: The commercial overlay assigned to the tax lot.

columns.name: Commercial Overlay 2
columns.description: A commercial overlay associated with the tax lot.

columns.name: Special District 1
columns.description: The special purpose district assigned to the tax lot.

columns.name: Special District 2
columns.description: The special purpose district assigned to the tax lot.

columns.name: Special District 3
columns.description: The special purpose district assigned to the tax lot.

columns.name: Limited Height District
columns.description: The limited height district assigned to the tax lot.

columns.name: Zoning Map Number
columns.description:
The Department of City Planning Zoning Map Number associated with
the tax lot's X and Y Coordinates.

columns.name: Zoning Map Code
columns.description:
A code (Y) identifies a border Tax Lot, i.e., a Tax Lot on that might
be on the border of two or more Zoning Maps.

dataset.name: Multiple Dwelling Registrations
dataset.description:
Pursuant to New York City’s Housing Maintenance Code, the Department of Housing 
Preservation and Development (HPD) collects registration information from owners of 
residential rental units. Owners are required to register if they own residential buildings 
with three or more units or if they own one- or two-family homes and neither they nor 
members of their immediate family live there. Registrations are required upon taking 
ownership of a qualifying building, and once a year thereafter.

dataset.name: Affordable Housing Production by Building
dataset.description: The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) reports on projects, buildings, and units that began after January 1, 2014, and are counted towards either the Housing New York plan (1/1/2014 – 12/31/2021) or the Housing Our Neighbors: A Blueprint for Housing & Homelessness plan (1/1/2022 – present).
dataset.department: Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD)
dataset.publisher: Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD)

columns.name: Project ID
columns.description: The Project ID is a unique numeric identifier assigned to each project by HPD.

columns.name: Census Tract
columns.description: The Census Tract indicates the 2010 U.S. Census Tract where the building is located.

columns.name: Latitude (Internal)
columns.description: The Latitude (Internal) and Longitude (Internal) specify the location of the property on the earth’s surface. The coordinates provided are of the internal centroid derived from the tax lot.

columns.name: Reporting Construction Type
columns.description: The Reporting Construction Type field indicates whether the building is categorized as ‘new construction’ or ‘preservation’ in Housing New York statistics. Note that some preservation projects included here may not actually involve construction, because they extend the project’s regulatory restrictions but do not require rehabilitation.

columns.name: BBL
columns.description: The BBL (Borough, Block, and Lot) is a unique identifier for each tax lot in the City.

columns.name: BIN
columns.description: The BIN (Building Identification Number) is a unique identifier for each building in the City.

columns.name: Number
columns.description: The House Number is the street number in the building’s address. E.g., the house number is ‘100’ in ‘100 Gold Street.’

columns.name: Extremely Low Income Units
columns.description: Extremely Low Income Units are units with rents that are affordable to households earning 0 to 30% of the area median income (AMI).

columns.name: 3-BR Units
columns.description: 3-BR Units are units with 3-bedrooms.

columns.name: Community Board
columns.description: The Community Board field indicates the New York City Community District where the building is located.

columns.name: Longitude (Internal)
columns.description: The Latitude (Internal) and Longitude (Internal) specify the location of the property on the earth’s surface. The coordinates provided are of the internal centroid derived from the tax lot.

columns.name: Project Name
columns.description: The Project Name is the name assigned to the project by HPD.

columns.name: Project Start Date
columns.description: The Project Start Date is the date of the project loan closing and regulatory agreement — or the notice of intent to market affordable units.

columns.name: Project Completion Date
columns.description: The Project Completion Date is the date that the last building in the project was completed. If the project has not yet completed, then the field is blank.

columns.name: Postcode
columns.description: Zip code

columns.name: NTA - Neighborhood Tabulation Area
columns.description: The Neighborhood Tabulation Area indicates the New York City Neighborhood Tabulation Area where the building is located.

columns.name: Longitude
columns.description: The Latitude and Longitude specify the location of the property on the earth’s surface. The coordinates provided are an estimate of the location based on the street segment and address range.

columns.name: Building Completion Date
columns.description: The Building Completion Date is the date the building was completed. The field is blank if the building has not completed.

columns.name: Moderate Income Units
columns.description: Moderate Income Units are units with rents that are affordable to households earning 81 to 120% of the area median income (AMI).

columns.name: Middle Income Units
columns.description: Middle Income Units are units with rents that are affordable to households earning 121 to 165% of the area median income (AMI).

columns.name: 1-BR Units
columns.description: 1-BR Units are units with 1-bedroom.

columns.name: Unknown-BR Units
columns.description: Unknown-BR Units are units with an unknown number of bedrooms.

columns.name: Studio Units
columns.description: Studio Units are units with 0-bedrooms.

columns.name: Other Income Units
columns.description: Other Units are units reserved for building superintendents.

columns.name: Low Income Units
columns.description: Low Income Units are units with rents that are affordable to households earning 51 to 80% of the area median income (AMI).

columns.name: Latitude
columns.description: The Latitude and Longitude specify the location of the property on the earth’s surface. The coordinates provided are an estimate of the location based on the street segment and address range.

columns.name: All Counted Units
columns.description: The Counted Units field indicates the total number of affordable units, counted towards the Housing New York plan, that are in the building.

columns.name: 5-BR Units
columns.description: 5-BR Units are units with 5-bedrooms.

columns.name: Building ID
columns.description: The Building ID is a unique numeric identifier assigned to each building by HPD.

columns.name: Street
columns.description: The Street Name is the name of the street in the building’s address. E.g., the street name is ‘Gold Street’ in ‘100 Gold Street.’

columns.name: Counted Homeownership Units
columns.description: Counted Homeownership Units are the units in the building, counted toward the Housing New York Plan, where assistance has been provided directly to homeowners.

columns.name: 2-BR Units
columns.description: 2-BR Units are units with 2-bedrooms.

columns.name: Counted Rental Units
columns.description: Counted Rental Units are the units in the building, counted toward the Housing New York plan, where assistance has been provided to landlords in exchange for a requirement for affordable units.

columns.name: Extended Affordability Only
columns.description: The Extended Affordability Only field indicates whether the project is considered to be Extended Affordability. An extended affordability project involves no construction, but secures an extended or new regulatory agreement. All extended affordability projects have a ‘reporting construction type’ of ‘preservation.’

columns.name: Prevailing Wage Status
columns.description: The Prevailing Wage Status field indicates whether the project is subject to prevailing wage requirements, such as Davis Bacon.

columns.name: Council District
columns.description: The Council District indicates the New York City Council District where the building is located.

columns.name: 4-BR Units
columns.description: 4-BR Units are units with 4-bedrooms.

columns.name: Total Units
columns.description: The Total Units field indicates the total number of units, affordable and market rate, in each building.

columns.name: Very Low Income Units
columns.description: Very Low Income Units are units with rents that are affordable to households earning 31 to 50% of the area median income (AMI).

columns.name: 6-BR+ Units
columns.description: 6-BR+ Units are units with 6-bedrooms or more.

columns.name: Borough
columns.description: The Borough is the borough where the building is located.
